newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London finished higher on persistent buying. November ended $30 higher at $1,540, while January closed $46 per tonne higher to end at $1,455 per tonne. There was no fresh fundamental reason for the rise but traders said persistent tight nearby supplies especially in the United States gave some background support. New York had another extremely strong session with prices rallying to about 6- months highs and causing the December/March spread to widen even further. December added 3.05 cents/lb to close at 127.35 cents/lb while March gained 95 points to close at 112.35 cents/lb. The outer months ended 50 points higher to 50 points lower. What is driving the market higher continues to be a lack of deliverable supplies, roaster support and little to no physical coffee available until later in the year.

Traders said producers have been selling March forward but there seems to be virtually no coffee around for the spot contract no matter how wide the spread. It was added that earlier talk of Mexican coffee showing up against the board seems to have been discredited by the market. It was said that with higher physical premiums being paid above futures, it is hard to justify coffee coming to the board no matter how wide the spread gets.

FUNDAMENTALS - PHILIPPINES - Coffee production in the Philippines in 1996/97 (July/June) is forecast to reach 983,000 60-bags, up from 849,000 bags produced the previous year. The 1995/96 figure is below earlier industry estimates of 937,000 bags.

EL SALVADOR - According to the Salvadorean Foundation of Coffee Investigation (PROCAFE) coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) could reach 2.346 million 60-kg bags, up from 2.325 million bags produced the previous year in spite of a 5 per cent loss of beans from earlier expectations due to rain damage at the start of the year. The estimate is based on a sample survey in the different coffee growing zones of the country which has a total of 16,191 plantations. The forecast only differs insignificantly from the recent forecast given by the Salvadorean Coffee Council.

AUSTRALIA - Australia imported 653,700 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 2.3 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.4 percent to 815,000 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Indonesia (102,100 vs 78,300 bags), Vietnam (137,100 vs 142,200 bags) and Papua/New Guinea (185,200 vs 154,900 bags).
